newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany seeks EU ban on feed antibiotic.
newsitem.headline: Germany seeks EU ban on feed antibiotic.

text.p: German farm minister Jochen Borchert is seeking a ban on the use of the antibiotic avoparcin in animal feed throughout the European Union, a farm ministry statement said on Thursday.

Borchert was renewing unsuccessful attempts earlier this year to widen a ban applied by some member countries to the whole of the EU, citing fears that the growth-boosting additive might create resistance to antibiotics in humans.
"If we waited for ultimate scientific evidence in the case of this important health issue, it could be a fatal mistake," Borchert was quoted as saying.
A ministry official said Borchert had written to EU farm ministers and Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler to explain his position.
Denmark, Germany, Sweden, Austria, Norway and Finland were applying national bans on avoparcin, he added.

Farm union DBV in a seperate statement said an EU-wide ban was necessary to create equal conditions for European livestock industries and to protect consumers in countries where a ban was in place but meat was imported from elsewhere.
